front_matter.title: Exact window Sugawara identity and Luttinger normal modes of tower density waves
front_matter.subject: quantum-fields

extraction.note: Attack on the target bos.dynamics: the dynamics of the density-wave bosons of the tower (Sugawara form, linear dispersion, solvable density-density interaction), derived in the Clifford algebra of the tower planes. The store held the Sugawara construction only as an imported conformal-field-theory Fact (dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction); it is not a premise here. Stored and used: the current algebra with its edge split (hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split), the density modes of a window and the canonical relations on the domain D of finite excitations of the band of the null vacuum (synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum (v), (vi)), and the null vacuum itself (synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator). New to the store: (i) the Sugawara (Kronig) identity holds on every finite window as an identity in the algebra, with no edge correction: sum_q rho_q* rho_q = sum_j j n_j - Nhat(Nhat - 1)/2, equivalently H = Q^2/2 + sum_q rho_q* rho_q for the half-integer weights about the sea; the edge operators that spoil the canonical commutator on a window cancel in this ordering; and an energy sum_j eps_j n_j is a multiple of sum_q rho_q* rho_q plus a function of the number exactly when eps is affine; (ii) linear dispersion and the phase flow of the density modes with the kernel unit J of a tower level; (iii) the compression of the null momentum P to the band modes has the half-integer weights Delta (k + 1/2), the null vacuum's window sea is the ground state of the compressed energy, and on D the infinite-band energy is Q^2/2 + sum_q rho_q* rho_q; (iv) a Luttinger-type density coupling between two families of modes of opposite orientation, with coupling constants on finitely many wave numbers, keeps the Heisenberg equations of the density modes linear on D, with real normal modes and frequencies q sqrt((1 + g4)^2 - g2^2), and on windows exactly on the edge-clean vectors. Prior art, not premises: the identity H = Q^2/2 + sum rho* rho on the infinite filled sea is the Kronig identity of bosonisation (R. de L. Kronig, Physica 2 (1935) 968-980, cited from memory) and the Sugawara construction (H. Sugawara, Phys. Rev. 170 (1968) 1659-1662, cited from memory); the solution of the density-coupled model is D. C. Mattis and E. H. Lieb, J. Math. Phys. 6 (1965) 304-312 (as cited in the stored Fact synthesis.imported-schwinger-term-and-mattis-lieb-density-algebra) and F. D. M. Haldane, J. Phys. C 14 (1981) 2585-2609 (cited from memory). For finitely many fermions on levels bounded below the identity is in K. Schoenhammer and V. Meden, Fermion-boson transmutation and comparison of statistical ensembles in one dimension, Am. J. Phys. (1996), doi:10.1119/1.18339, eq. (38); the window form, with an upper cut-off as well, follows by the same antisymmetry and is new to the store, not to the literature. The half-integer offset of the weight clause of singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave (version 3), read in the store as a reading of the modes as spinors of boost weight 1/2, appears in (iii) as the band centre of the compression; this is recorded, not used to change that premise. Not claimed: the compression in (iii) is not invariant under the null translations (the band modes are not eigenvectors of P), so (iii) is a statement about the compressed energy and the null vacuum restricted to the band modes, not about the full dynamics of the generator; the families of (iv) are not identified with particular generators; no gauge boson is constructed. Ledger: (i), (ii) and (iv) are transport-absent (finite CAR algebra of tower planes); (iii) is transport-convenient (the generator's mode space and its null vacuum).

levels.formal:
Let a window carry $L$ tower planes with null pairs $v_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} + f_{j})$, $w_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} - f_{j})$, $Q(e_{j}) = 1$, $Q(f_{j}) = -1$, $j = 0, \dots, L - 1$, the Witt pairs of Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} read with $v_{j}$ as creators, $n_{j} = v_{j}w_{j}$, $\hat N = \sum_{j}n_{j}$, $*$ the adjoint ($v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$), and the density modes $\rho_{q} = \sum_{j = 0}^{L - 1 - q}v_{j}w_{j + q}$, $1 \le q \le L - 1$, of Theorem \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} (each lowers the level index by $q$). Let $T = \sum_{q = 1}^{L - 1}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Window Sugawara identity.)} For every $L$, exactly,
\[
T = \sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1).
\]
For $L = 2M$, with $k = j - M$, the half-integer weights $k + \tfrac12$, the sea $k < 0$ filled, $H = \sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} + \tfrac12M^{2}$ and $\mathcal{Q} = \hat N - M$, this reads $H = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + T$: $H$ vanishes on the sea and is at least $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$. There is no edge correction, although $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$ is the edge operator of the stored result. An energy $\sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j}n_{j}$ equals $aT + g(\hat N)$ for a real $a$ and a function $g$ if and only if $\varepsilon_{j} = aj + b$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Linear dispersion and the phase flow.)} $[H, \rho_{q}^{*}] = q\rho_{q}^{*}$ and $[H, \rho_{q}] = -q\rho_{q}$ exactly. In a tower level $\Cl(L, L + 2)$ with kernel bivector $J = g_{1}g_{2}$ ($J^{2} = -1$, commuting with every plane generator), $e^{JtH} = e^{JtM^{2}/2}\prod_{k}\bigl(1 + (e^{Jt(k + 1/2)} - 1)n_{k}\bigr)$ is unitary for real $t$ and $e^{JtH}\rho_{q}^{*}e^{-JtH} = e^{Jqt}\rho_{q}^{*}$: every density wave of wave number $q$ turns at frequency $q$ with the unit $J$, whatever its position in the window.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The band of the null vacuum.)} On a horizon generator, with $P = I_{4}\,d/du$, the null vacuum $\omega_{0}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator} and the band modes $g_{k} = h_{k}\otimes\eta$ of width $\Delta$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi), $\ip{g_{k}}{Pg_{l}} = \delta_{kl}\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$: the compression of $P$ to the span of the band modes has the half-integer weights $\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$, and on the window $k = -M, \dots, M - 1$ its second quantisation is $\Delta\sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} = \Delta(H - \tfrac12M^{2})$. The restriction of $\omega_{0}$ to the window is the sea, the ground state of $H$, with $\mathcal{Q} = 0$ and $\rho_{q}$ annihilating it. On the domain $\mathcal{D}$ of finite excitations of the infinite band, $H_{\infty} = \sum_{k \ge 0}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} - \sum_{k < 0}(k + \tfrac12)(1 - n_{k})$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty} = \sum_{k \ge 0}n_{k} - \sum_{k < 0}(1 - n_{k})$ are finite sums on each vector, and on $\mathcal{D}$
\[
H_{\infty} = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^{2} + \sum_{q \ge 1}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q} = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^{2} + \sum_{q \ge 1}q\,b_{q}^{*}b_{q}, \qquad b_{q} = \rho_{q}/\sqrt q ,
\]
with $[b_{q}, b_{q'}^{*}] = \delta_{qq'}$ on $\mathcal{D}$: in each charge sector the energy is that of free bosons of frequency $q$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Luttinger coupling.)} Take two families of window modes, $R$ with weights $k + \tfrac12$ and sea $k < 0$, and $L$ with weights $-(k + \tfrac12)$ and sea $k \ge 0$, with density modes $\rho_{R, q} = \sum_{k}v_{R, k}w_{R, k + q}$ and $\rho_{L, q} = \sum_{k}v_{L, k + q}w_{L, k}$, both lowering the energy by $q$. For a finite set $S$ of wave numbers and real $g_{4, q}$, $g_{2, q}$ ($q \in S$) with $|g_{2, q}| < 1 + g_{4, q}$, let
\[
H = H_{R} + H_{L} + \sum_{q \in S}\Bigl[g_{4, q}\bigl(\rho_{R, q}^{*}\rho_{R, q} + \rho_{L, q}^{*}\rho_{L, q}\bigr) + g_{2, q}\bigl(\rho_{R, q}\rho_{L, q} + \rho_{L, q}^{*}\rho_{R, q}^{*}\bigr)\Bigr],
\]
$r_{q}$ the root of $g_{2, q}r^{2} - 2(1 + g_{4, q})r + g_{2, q} = 0$ with $|r_{q}| < 1$, $\beta_{q}^{*} = \rho_{R, q}^{*} + r_{q}\rho_{L, q}$, $\gamma_{q}^{*} = \rho_{L, q}^{*} + r_{q}\rho_{R, q}$ and $\omega_{q} = q\sqrt{(1 + g_{4, q})^{2} - g_{2, q}^{2}}$. On the domain $\mathcal{D}$ of finite excitations of both infinite seas, $H$ maps $\mathcal{D}$ into itself and
\[
[H, \beta_{q}^{*}] = \omega_{q}\beta_{q}^{*}, \qquad [H, \gamma_{q}^{*}] = \omega_{q}\gamma_{q}^{*} ;
\]
the Heisenberg equations of the density modes close linearly, with real coefficients. On finite windows the same relations hold exactly on every vector whose two families are edge-clean at depth $\max S$, and do not hold on every vector off that subspace (the check exhibits one where they fail; on others, such as the vector with both families empty, they still hold).
\end{enumerate}
All clauses are proved. \emph{Reading.} The kinetic energy of fermions with linear dispersion is already, on every finite window and with no edge correction, the quadratic form of the density waves plus the charge term $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$; the finite size shows only in the commutators of the density modes, not in this energy. Density-density couplings keep the dynamics quadratic in the density waves and so solvable.
levels.technical:
On a window of tower planes, let $\rho_{q}$ move one fermion $q$ levels down. The sum $T = \sum_{q}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$ equals $\sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$ exactly, as an identity in the algebra, on every window: the kinetic energy of fermions with equally spaced levels is the quadratic form of the density waves, and with the levels $k + \tfrac12$ about the sea it is $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + T$, the Sugawara (Kronig) form with the charge term. The finite window shows only in $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$, which is an edge operator; the energy identity itself has no edge term. The identity needs the linear dispersion: an energy is a multiple of $T$ plus a function of the number exactly when its levels are equally spaced.

Each density wave of wave number $q$ raises the energy by exactly $q$, wherever it sits, so with the kernel unit $J$ of a tower level the flow $e^{JtH}$ turns $\rho_{q}^{*}$ at frequency $q$. On a horizon generator, compressing the null momentum to the band modes of width $\Delta$ gives exactly the weights $\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$, the half-integer offset being the band centre; the null vacuum restricted to the bands is the sea, the ground state, and on the finite excitations of the infinite band the energy is $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + \sum_{q}q\,b_{q}^{*}b_{q}$ with canonical $b_{q}$.

Coupling two families of opposite orientation through their densities, with constants $g_{4}$ (within a family) and $g_{2}$ (between them) on finitely many wave numbers, keeps the Heisenberg equations of the densities linear; real normal modes $\rho_{R}^{*} + r\rho_{L}$ have frequencies $q\sqrt{(1 + g_{4})^{2} - g_{2}^{2}}$. On windows this holds exactly on the vectors that are edge-clean at the coupled depth.
levels.lay: Fermions on a line whose energy levels are equally spaced have a hidden description: their energy can be rewritten exactly as the energy of ripples in their density, plus a term that only counts how many fermions were added or removed. This is the core of how fermions in one dimension turn into bosons. The result shows that the rewriting holds exactly even for a finite stretch of levels, with nothing to correct at the ends, provided the spacing is even. Each ripple then carries an energy proportional to its wavelength number, which is what a sound wave does. When the ripples of two streams moving in opposite directions push on each other, the motion stays simple: new combined ripples form with a changed common speed (slower or faster, depending on the two couplings), and the problem can still be solved exactly. On a horizon line the lowest-energy state the series uses is the state with no ripples.
levels.one-liner: On every window of tower planes $\sum_{q}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q} = \sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$ exactly, so $\sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} + \tfrac12M^{2} = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + \sum_{q}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$ with no edge term; density waves have frequency $q$ (unit $J$), and a Luttinger density coupling gives real normal modes of frequency $q\sqrt{(1 + g_{4})^{2} - g_{2}^{2}}$.

proofs.main:
\emph{Preliminaries.} By Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} the $v_{j}, w_{j}$ satisfy $v_{j}^{2} = w_{j}^{2} = 0$, $\{v_{j}, w_{k}\} = \delta_{jk}$ and distinct planes' generators anticommute; $n_{j} = v_{j}w_{j}$ are commuting idempotents with $[n_{l}, v_{j}] = \delta_{lj}v_{j}$ and $[n_{l}, w_{j}] = -\delta_{lj}w_{j}$, and $\hat Nw_{j} = w_{j}(\hat N - 1)$. Theorem \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} gives, on a window, $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q}^{*}] = \sum_{k < q}n_{k} - \sum_{k \ge L - q}n_{k}$, $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q'}] = 0$, and for $q \ne q'$ a cross commutator $[\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$ supported on the lowest and highest $\max(q, q')$ modes that annihilates every vector edge-clean at that depth (the lowest $\max(q, q')$ modes filled, the highest empty).

\emph{(i)} Moving $w_{j}$ past $v_{j'}$, $\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q} = \sum_{j, j'}v_{j + q}w_{j}v_{j'}w_{j' + q} = \sum_{j}n_{j + q} - \sum_{j, j'}v_{j + q}v_{j'}w_{j}w_{j' + q}$. Summed over $q \ge 1$, the first term counts each $n_{l}$ once for every $q$ with $1 \le q \le l$, giving $\sum_{l}l\,n_{l}$. In the second, write $\alpha = j + q$, $\beta = j'$, $\gamma = j$, $\delta = j' + q$: the sum over $q \ge 1$ and $j, j'$ is the sum $X$ of $v_{\alpha}v_{\beta}w_{\gamma}w_{\delta}$ over the quadruples in the window with $\alpha + \beta = \gamma + \delta$ and $\alpha > \gamma$, each once. Let $S$ be the same sum over all quadruples with $\alpha + \beta = \gamma + \delta$. Renaming $\gamma \leftrightarrow \delta$ preserves the index set and $w_{\gamma}w_{\delta} = -w_{\delta}w_{\gamma}$, so $S = -S = 0$. The part with $\alpha < \gamma$ has $\beta > \delta$, and the renaming $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta) \mapsto (\beta, \alpha, \delta, \gamma)$ maps it onto the part with $\alpha > \gamma$, with the sign $(-1)^{2} = 1$: it equals $X$. The part with $\alpha = \gamma$ (then $\beta = \delta$) is $D = \sum_{\alpha, \beta}v_{\alpha}v_{\beta}w_{\alpha}w_{\beta} = -\sum_{\alpha}v_{\alpha}\hat Nw_{\alpha} = -\sum_{\alpha}v_{\alpha}w_{\alpha}(\hat N - 1) = -\hat N(\hat N - 1)$. So $0 = 2X + D$, $X = \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$ and $T = \sum_{l}l\,n_{l} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$. With $j = k + M$, $H = \sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - (M - \tfrac12)\hat N + \tfrac12M^{2} = T + \tfrac12\hat N^{2} - M\hat N + \tfrac12M^{2} = T + \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$. On the sea every $\rho_{q}$ vanishes (a fermion at $j + q$ would have to drop to an empty level $j < j + q$, and in the sea every level below a filled one is filled) and $\mathcal{Q} = 0$, so $H = 0$ there; $T$ is a sum of elements $\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$, nonnegative in every state, so $H \ge \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$. If $\varepsilon_{j} = aj + b$, then $\sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j}n_{j} = aT + \tfrac{a}{2}\hat N(\hat N - 1) + b\hat N$. Conversely, on the one-particle vector $v_{j}\Omega_{0}$ ($\Omega_{0} = \prod_{l}w_{l}v_{l}$ the empty projector), $T$ acts as $j$ by the identity and $g(\hat N)$ as $g(1)$, so $\varepsilon_{j} = aj + g(1)$. The check verifies the identity as an equality of elements of $\Cl(L, L)$ for $L = 1, \dots, 6$, the sea form for even $L$, the one-particle values of $T$, and that weights $j^{2}$ are not of this form for $L \ge 3$.

\emph{(ii)} From $[n_{l}, v_{j}w_{j + q}] = (\delta_{lj} - \delta_{l, j + q})v_{j}w_{j + q}$, $[\sum_{l}\varepsilon_{l}n_{l}, \rho_{q}] = \sum_{j}(\varepsilon_{j} - \varepsilon_{j + q})v_{j}w_{j + q} = -q\rho_{q}$ for $\varepsilon_{l} = l + c$, and the adjoint gives $[H, \rho_{q}^{*}] = q\rho_{q}^{*}$. In $\Cl(L, L + 2)$, $J$ commutes with the plane generators and $J^{2} = -1$, so $e^{Jt\varepsilon n_{k}} = 1 + (e^{Jt\varepsilon} - 1)n_{k}$, the factors commute, and $(e^{JtH})^{*} = e^{-JtH}$ ($J^{*} = -J$, $H^{*} = H$). Since $J$ commutes with $H$ and $\rho_{q}^{*}$, $\operatorname{ad}(JtH)\rho_{q}^{*} = Jqt\,\rho_{q}^{*}$, and summing the exponential series of $\operatorname{ad}$ gives $e^{JtH}\rho_{q}^{*}e^{-JtH} = e^{Jqt}\rho_{q}^{*}$. The check verifies the commutators for $L = 2, 3, 4$, unitarity, and the phase $e^{Jqt}$ at the Pythagorean point $e^{Jt/2} = \tfrac35 + \tfrac45J$, and that weights $j^{2}$ give no such relation.

\emph{(iii)} In the $P$-spectral representation $h_{k}$ is $\Delta^{-1/2}$ times the indicator of $[k\Delta, (k + 1)\Delta)$, so $\ip{h_{k}}{Ph_{l}} = 0$ for $k \ne l$ (disjoint supports) and $\ip{h_{k}}{Ph_{k}} = \Delta^{-1}\int_{k\Delta}^{(k + 1)\Delta}p\,dp = \Delta(k + \tfrac12)$; tensoring with the unit vector $\eta$ changes nothing. The compression is therefore diagonal on the $g_{k}$ with these weights, and its second quantisation on the window is $\Delta\sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k}$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi) the restriction of $\omega_{0}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii), symbol $\chi_{(-\infty, 0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$) to the band modes is the product state with $n_{k} = 1$ for $k < 0$ and $0$ for $k \ge 0$, the sea, on which $H = 0$ and $\rho_{q} = 0$ by (i). On $\mathcal{D}$: a vector $\psi = x\Omega$ with $x$ a polynomial in modes of $[-K, K)$ is a combination of occupation vectors that agree with the sea outside $[-K, K)$. On such a vector $\rho_{q}$ acts only through terms $v_{k}w_{k + q}$ with $k \ge -K$ empty and $k + q < K$ filled, so it vanishes for $q \ge 2K$ and keeps the support in $[-K, K)$; $\rho_{q}^{*}$ acts through terms $v_{k + q}w_{k}$ with $k < K$ filled and $k + q \ge -K$ empty, so its result agrees with the sea outside $[-K - q, K + q)$. Hence on $\psi$ every operator in the display involves only modes of the window $[-3K, 3K)$ and coincides there with the window operators of (i) for $M = 3K$; $H_{\infty}\psi = H\psi$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}\psi = \mathcal{Q}\psi$ because the modes outside the window contribute $0$ to the normal-ordered sums on $\psi$. Identity (i) is an identity in the algebra of the window, so it holds in the representation of $\omega_{0}$, and gives $H_{\infty}\psi = (\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^{2} + \sum_{q \ge 1}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q})\psi$, the sum finite on $\psi$. The canonical relations $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q'}^{*}] = q\delta_{qq'}$ on $\mathcal{D}$ are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi). The check computes the band means $\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$ exactly for three widths and eight bands, the band occupations of the null vacuum, and $H = 0$, $\rho_{q} = 0$ on the window sea.

\emph{(iv)} The relabelling $k \mapsto -1 - k$ of the $L$ family maps its weights $-(k + \tfrac12)$, its sea $k \ge 0$ and its density modes $\rho_{L, q}$ to the weights, sea and density modes of an $R$ family, so the results above hold for both families. Operators of different families commute (even elements on disjoint planes). For one $q \in S$ and a vector $\psi$, compute with $[\rho^{*}_{q'}\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}^{*}] = \rho_{q'}^{*}[\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$ (as $[\rho_{q'}^{*}, \rho_{q}^{*}] = 0$) and $[\rho_{q'}^{*}\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}] = [\rho_{q'}^{*}, \rho_{q}]\rho_{q'}$:
\[
[H, \rho_{R, q}^{*}] = q\rho_{R, q}^{*} + \sum_{q' \in S}\bigl(g_{4, q'}\rho_{R, q'}^{*}[\rho_{R, q'}, \rho_{R, q}^{*}] + g_{2, q'}[\rho_{R, q'}, \rho_{R, q}^{*}]\rho_{L, q'}\bigr),
\]
\[
[H, \rho_{L, q}] = -q\rho_{L, q} - \sum_{q' \in S}\bigl(g_{4, q'}[\rho_{L, q}, \rho_{L, q'}^{*}]\rho_{L, q'} + g_{2, q'}[\rho_{L, q}, \rho_{L, q'}^{*}]\rho_{R, q'}^{*}\bigr).
\]
On $\mathcal{D}$ the brackets are $q\delta_{qq'}$ and every operator maps $\mathcal{D}$ into itself ($S$ is finite), so $[H, \rho_{R, q}^{*}] = q(1 + g_{4, q})\rho_{R, q}^{*} + qg_{2, q}\rho_{L, q}$ and $[H, \rho_{L, q}] = -q(1 + g_{4, q})\rho_{L, q} - qg_{2, q}\rho_{R, q}^{*}$. Then $[H, \beta_{q}^{*}] = q\bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - r_{q}g_{2, q}\bigr)\rho_{R, q}^{*} + q\bigl(g_{2, q} - r_{q}(1 + g_{4, q})\bigr)\rho_{L, q}$, which is a multiple of $\beta_{q}^{*}$ exactly when $g_{2, q} - r_{q}(1 + g_{4, q}) = r_{q}\bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - r_{q}g_{2, q}\bigr)$, the stated quadratic. Its roots are real and distinct with product $1$ when $|g_{2, q}| < 1 + g_{4, q}$; the one of modulus less than $1$ is $r_{q} = \bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - \sqrt{(1 + g_{4, q})^{2} - g_{2, q}^{2}}\bigr)/g_{2, q}$ ($r_{q} = 0$ if $g_{2, q} = 0$), and the multiple is $q\bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - r_{q}g_{2, q}\bigr) = \omega_{q}$. Exchanging the roles of $R$ and $L$ gives $[H, \gamma_{q}^{*}] = \omega_{q}\gamma_{q}^{*}$. On a window, let $\psi$ be edge-clean at depth $\max S$ in both families (for $L$, in the relabelled order). The brackets in the displays act either on $\psi$, or on $\rho_{L, q'}\psi$ or $\rho_{R, q'}^{*}\psi$, which have the other family's occupations of $\psi$, or, for $[\rho_{L, q}, \rho_{L, q'}^{*}]\rho_{L, q'}\psi$, on $\rho_{L, q'}\psi$, which is still edge-clean in $L$ (a lowering density mode cannot fill an empty edge level of its own family or empty a filled one); so by the stored edge identities every bracket acts as $q\delta_{qq'}$ there and the computation above holds on $\psi$. The check verifies $[H, \beta^{*}]\psi = \tfrac65\beta^{*}\psi$ and $[H, \gamma^{*}]\psi = \tfrac65\gamma^{*}\psi$ for $S = \{1\}$, $g_{4} = \tfrac12$, $g_{2} = \tfrac{9}{10}$, $r = \tfrac13$, on all sixteen depth-one edge-clean vectors of two four-mode families, and that the relation fails on a vector that is not edge-clean.
